```regex
^([01]\d|2[0-3]):[0-5]\d$
```

- `^` and `$` anchor the match to the whole line, so extra text on either side fails.
- `[01]\d` covers hours 00–19, and `2[0-3]` covers 20–23. Together they accept exactly 00–23.
- `[0-5]\d` accepts minutes 00–59.

This requires two digits for the hour, so `7:45` won't match. If you want to accept single-digit hours, use `^([01]?\d|2[0-3]):[0-5]\d$`.

To test it with grep, use `grep -E '^([01]\d|2[0-3]):[0-5]\d$'`. Some engines, such as POSIX `grep` without `-P`, don't support `\d`, so use `[0-9]` there: `^([01][0-9]|2[0-3]):[0-5][0-9]$`.
